column1: # What Phiogy looks like: kind, token, value. One ink on one ground, and
# one light that every surface wears (puikit's: src/tokens/tokens.scss).
# The light: its colour, how much of it the strongest shade is, and the
# share of that a shade at rest and a soft one have. A surface is lit
# from its foot (0 degrees: the light fades upward), a label from its
# left (90: it fades to the right). Nothing has a fill of its own.
# No glass: the window is opaque and its panes stand on its ground. A
# look that is glass says otherwise (data/look.tsv).
# The column down the middle of the body, which every part there keeps
# to; and the mark that ends a text cut short.
# The window's own furniture, which appkit draws: the activity bar, the
# user's mark, the tabs, a modal's panel, the profile.
# The bar is `activity.low` thick, and a menu beside it `activity.width`
# wide (puikit's shell: a rail of icons and a panel).
# It stands clear of the window's top, foot and side, its corners round.
# The caption: the row at the window's very top, where a system puts
# its title bar. It has the app's mark over the bar, its name, and the
# pin that puts the bar's menu away and brings it back. On Windows it
# stands in the system's bar's place and has the window's three
# A modal is a square that fills half of the window's space, and never
# more of its shorter side than the share given: at a desk, in a hand.
# A modal that is a drawer stands at the right edge, this wide; one that
# is a sheet lies at the foot, this share of the window high and no
# wider than this. Both stay a margin clear of the window's edges.
# What appkit's field and button ask for, in a part that has one.
# The mark drawn in place of each character of a password.
# The foot of a room, where the line says where it is.
# A room: how high a row of who is on its line is, how round its
# light, and how wide the mark before a name.
# The hosts: how far down their heading is, and how high a host's row.
# A caller this window is connected to: how wide the bar that shows
# how loud they are is at its loudest, and how high.
# A call over a room's stream, as the web's stands there: how wide a
# camera's tile is at most (15rem) and a screen's (24rem), how high
# each is for its width (4 to 3, 16 to 9), how large a face is, the
# most of the stream's height a call takes, how loud a caller is, as
# a share of full, to count as heard; and, where the tiles would need
# more height than that, the share of its size each keeps at every
# step smaller, down to the least.
# How wide the room for a name under a tile is at least.
# A room: how wide its part must be for its people to stand beside what
# was said, how wide they stand there, and the share of its height they
# have where they stand over it.
# Pictures. A face beside a message and in a direct room's title; a
# picture posted in a room, how wide and how high; a place's mark; and
# the viewer: the face of who posted it, a picture of its strip, the
# square a control that stands alone is in (the way out, an arrow), a
# tool, how thick the mark around the picture shown is in the strip,
# and how many times the width of its room a picture shown larger is.
# They are the web's: 2.75rem, 2.75rem less 0.5rem, 2px, twice.
# A page that is a list (the hosts, friends, finding people, the
# shops, the bag): how far down it begins, how high a line of it is,
# and how large what stands at a line's head; and how many hosts and
# how many people a search lists at most, as on the web.
# The shops: how many a search lists at most; how wide a card of a
# grid is; how many times as wide as high a landing's picture is; the
# widest a thing's picture is on its own page; and how many more like
# it are shown there, as on the web.
# A person beside the room: how large their face is, how many times
# as wide as high the picture over their profile is (the web's 3/1),
# and how many of their pictures stand in a row.
